papers.title: Somnus, a tunable, open-source platform for automated EEG sleep scoring in physiological and disease mouse models
papers.summary: Somnus is an open-source Python platform for automated sleep staging in rodents using EEG, EMG, and optional video. Its base model, trained across diverse recordings from six laboratories, enables rapid fine-tuning via a graphical interface that targets uncertain epochs, allowing accurate custom scorers for disease models with minimal manual correction.

papers.title: What EEG doesn't see: a whole-brain MEG map of sleep spindles and slow oscillations
papers.summary: Simultaneous MEG/EEG during daytime naps in 19 young adults showed that sleep spindles and slow oscillations occur throughout the brain, including thalamus, hippocampus, and cerebellum, with region-specific balances between fast/slow spindles and SO frequency bands. A single scalp derivation (Cz-M1) provides a selective and partly composite view: more SOs were detected in every brain region than at Cz-M1, whereas fast spindles were more frequent at Cz-M1 than in any single source region.

papers.title: Predicting ICU Seizures Using 1 hour of cEEG.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.summary: An automated interpretable pipeline using one hour of ICU cEEG estimated near-term seizure risk from interictal-ictal continuum probabilities and quantitative background features in 50 adults. For the 4-hour horizon, a combined-feature SVM achieved 76% accuracy and Brier score 0.25, and accuracy declined from 94% at 1 hour to 79% at 24 hours, with initial external validation supporting generalizability.

papers.title: Distinct electroencephalography alpha-band rhythms map macroscale brain gradients.
papers.summary: Using source-reconstructed resting-state EEG from 608 adults (3,255 recordings), the study found that 38.3% of recordings had separable alpha-frequency components that aligned with canonical functional networks, especially separating visual and somatomotor systems. Low-dimensional analysis identified a sensory-differentiation axis and a sensorimotor-association axis resembling functional-connectomic gradients, linking split alpha to macroscale cortical organization.

papers.title: EEG Pathology Detection via Clinical Concept Bottleneck Models
papers.summary: This study introduces concept bottleneck models for EEG pathology detection that use analytically computed clinical EEG biomarkers (e.g., band power, spectral ratios, phase locking values) as an interpretable bottleneck. The models approach black-box baseline accuracy on TUAB (82.7-82.9% vs 83.6%) but show lower performance on CAUEEG (57.9-60.5% vs 62.7%), with a pure CBM variant exhibiting concept fidelity concerns mitigated by increasing concept loss weight.

papers.title: Fixed-Sequence OFF-to-ON Differences in Low-Beta State Dynamics in Parkinson's Disease: A Paired Source-Space Resting-State EEG Study.
papers.summary: In 39 Parkinson's disease patients with paired OFF/ON resting-state EEG, low-beta (13-20 Hz) dynamic amplitude-envelope connectivity showed higher switching rate and entropy in the later ON session compared to the earlier OFF session, with lower fractional occupancy and mean dwell time of an OFF-dominant state. The fixed OFF-then-ON protocol confounds medication state with session order, time, vigilance, fatigue, and adaptation, so medication-specific effects cannot be distinguished.

papers.title: Attenuated alpha state transitions and disrupted repetition-dependent temporal adaptation in mild cognitive impairment
papers.summary: In 77 participants with mild cognitive impairment and 60 healthy controls, occipital alpha (8-12 Hz) transitions during repeated eye-opening/eye-closure cycles were weaker and less successful in MCI, with no group difference in post-onset time constant. MCI showed absent repetition-dependent temporal adaptation: healthy controls developed later onset during eye opening and earlier onset during eye closure across trials, whereas MCI did not.

papers.title: Robust and replicable effects of ageing on resting-state brain electrophysiology measured with MEG.
papers.summary: Using the GLM-Spectrum on eyes-closed resting-state MEG, this study estimates a full-frequency whole-head profile of ageing effects that replicates across open-access datasets and is robust to common covariates. Distinct frequency components have different effect sizes, and the age effect is partially robust to grey matter volume modeling, showing that targeting an age effect linearly separable from a covariate can reduce statistical power.

papers.title: A Multi-Domain EEG Framework Integrating Spectral, Functional Connectivity, and Topological Features for Subject-Level ADHD Classification
papers.summary: The study developed an EEG classification framework for subject-level ADHD diagnosis by integrating spectral, functional connectivity (wPLI), and topological (persistent homology) features. Using SVM after recursive feature elimination, it achieved 80.17% accuracy and 86.72% ROC-AUC, with ablation showing multi-domain fusion outperformed single domains and explainable AI highlighting functional connectivity as the primary contributor.

papers.title: From Computational Models to Clinical Decision-Making in Epilepsy: Bridging the Gap Between Theory and Practice.
papers.summary: This review critically analyzes major international computational epileptology initiatives from 2004 to 2026, covering mechanistic biophysical models, AI/deep-learning predictive models, and digital brain twin or adaptive closed-loop systems, and evaluates their actual contribution to clinical decision-making. It argues that future progress depends on hybrid, explainable architectures that converge AI with mechanistic modeling rather than treating them as opposing approaches.

papers.title: Intracranial characterization of gamma in humans in response to auditory gratings
papers.summary: Intracranial recordings in seven epilepsy patients during auditory grating presentation showed a transient broadband gamma increase (30-100 Hz) followed by sustained beta suppression (14-28 Hz), with gamma selective for slower spectro-temporal modulations.

papers.title: Modulation of the speed of Intrinsic Alpha Frequency (IAF) with tACS modulates variability of illusory speech perception
papers.summary: Using tACS at intrinsic alpha frequency and ±2 Hz offsets over occipital electrodes in 27 healthy participants, this study found that tACS significantly reduced illusory /ta/ percepts in McGurk trials and that a Kuramoto-oscillator model explained the percentage of illusory responses.

papers.title: Brief Trains of Closed-loop TMS Induce Controllable Power in FM-theta Oscillations
papers.summary: This study locked brief rhythmic TMS trains to real-time frontal-midline theta phase in six healthy adults and found that trough-triggered, but not peak-triggered, trains transiently increased post-train FM-theta power (4.6-7.1 Hz) about 50-440 ms after stimulation, without affecting task performance.

papers.title: A touch that lingers: synchronized patting strengthens neural tracking of auditory rhythm in newborns
papers.summary: In 40 full-term newborns, high-density EEG showed that neural tracking of French lullabies was stronger when songs were accompanied by synchronized patting, and this enhancement persisted during subsequent periods without touch, especially in newborns with weaker auditory-only tracking.

papers.title: Acoustic Context Shapes Cortical Encoding of Spectral Discrimination in Normal and Impaired Hearing
papers.summary: This EEG study investigated how acoustic context and temporal-envelope variability shape cortical encoding of spectral contrast in normal-hearing and hearing-impaired listeners. The auditory change complex was larger and more symmetrical for discrete spectro-temporal modulations than conventional ones, decreased with spectral contrast, and was weaker and delayed in hearing-impaired listeners, while auditory steady-state responses remained contrast-insensitive.

papers.title: Simultaneous recordings link intracranial and scalp correlates of somatosensory awareness in humans
papers.summary: Using simultaneous high-density scalp EEG and intracranial EEG, this study links the scalp N140/somatosensory awareness negativity to insulo-opercular local field potentials following broadband high-frequency activity (50-150 Hz) after median nerve stimulation. The results identify the neural origins of the N140/SAN and connect scalp and intracranial correlates of somatosensory awareness.

papers.title: How aging reshapes implicit learning: behavioral and oscillatory evidence from an EEG-adapted Fast Mapping paradigm.
papers.summary: Used an EEG-adapted Fast Mapping paradigm (DIILT) in 31 younger and 35 older adults to test age-related changes in implicit learning, with a one-month delayed recognition measure. Younger adults rapidly acquired novel implicit associations and showed early posterior theta engagement for novel items, while older adults showed limited novel-item improvement and no such theta modulation; implicitly learned associations were retained after one month more stably than explicitly encoded ones in both groups.

papers.title: Advances in monitoring the injured brain.
papers.summary: Reviews recent advances in multimodal neuromonitoring for traumatic brain injury, covering invasive and non-invasive modalities such as brain tissue oxygenation, cerebral microdialysis, continuous EEG, near-infrared spectroscopy, and cerebrovascular autoregulation assessment. It highlights integration into multimodal platforms and the role of artificial intelligence and machine learning in data integration and prognostic modeling for precision neurocritical care.

papers.title: Motor effort biases perceptual decisions through later-stage evidence accumulation rather than early sensory-attentional processing
papers.summary: Recorded 64-channel EEG in 24 healthy adults performing an orientation discrimination task with two pressure-sensitive response buttons requiring different force levels to determine when motor effort biases perceptual decisions. Motor effort reduced pre-stimulus alpha power contralateral to the low-effort option and increased pre-response centro-parietal positivity for low-effort choices without altering early P1/N1 sensory responses, with trial-by-trial CPP amplitude predicting low-effort selection, indicating a later-stage evidence accumulation bias.

papers.title: A Novel Digital Phenotype of Physical Activity: Associations with Heart Rate Fragmentation
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 602 male veterans, Gaussian mixture modeling identified two overlapping physical activity phenotypes, compact-early and diffuse-late, based on accelerometry across six domains. The diffuse-late phenotype was associated with modestly higher heart rate fragmentation (PIP and IALS), suggesting a link between activity timing and neuroautonomic dysregulation.

papers.title: How do Uncompensated Micro-Shifts Systematically Confound Low-Concentration Metabolite Quantification in 1H-MRS Analysis?
papers.summary: Systematically evaluated how uncompensated frequency perturbations affect 1H-MRS linear combination model fitting using simulations and a public in vivo human brain dataset (n = 31). High-concentration metabolites showed minimal quantification changes, but low-concentration metabolites including Gln, GSH, Asp, and NAAG showed relative changes exceeding 10%-20%, often with CRLB values still within conventionally acceptable ranges, indicating that CRLB alone is insufficient for assessing quantification reliability.

papers.title: Large-scale all-optical electrophysiology links excitability and connectivity to circuit dynamics in vivo
papers.summary: Developed large-scale all-optical electrophysiology tools and applied them to approximately 300 layer 1 interneurons per mouse in vivo, identifying 1,469 inhibitory and 5,752 directed electrical connections among 14,312 tested pairs across two mice. Presynaptic identity was more strongly associated with IPSP amplitude and postsynaptic identity with IPSP decay time, and excitability under optogenetic stimulus predicted spontaneous spiking responses, linking cellular properties and pairwise interactions to circuit dynamics.

papers.title: Effects of morning versus evening high-intensity exercise on electroencephalographic and autonomic responses in middle-aged women.
papers.summary: Thirty middle-aged women (50-60 years) were randomized to morning (6:00 am) or evening (6:00 pm) high-intensity exercise, with EEG (TBR, SEF-90) and HRV-derived autonomic indices measured before and after exercise. Morning exercise produced greater pre-to-post changes in TBR, SEF-90, and sympathetic/parasympathetic HRV indices, suggesting time-of-day-dependent neurophysiological responses.

papers.title: Effects of Transcranial Photobiomodulation on Motor Functions in Healthy Individuals: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial, 60 healthy right-handed participants received active or sham transcranial photobiomodulation (850 nm, 36 J/cm2) over the supplementary motor area for four consecutive days. Active tPBM improved non-dominant hand motor performance (reduced reaction and movement times, increased accuracy) and increased resting alpha and beta power at C3 and C4 electrodes, with no significant changes in the sham group.

papers.title: Positive emotional synchrony and intimacy satisfaction: evidence from a multidimensional assessment.
papers.summary: Using behavioral coding, self-reports, and EEG hyperscanning during actual interactions, this study examined how emotional synchrony predicts intimacy satisfaction and tested self-other overlap as a mediator. Positive emotional synchrony directly predicted men's intimacy satisfaction with partial mediation by self-other overlap, while for women the effect on intimacy satisfaction was fully mediated by self-other overlap; interpersonal neural synchrony similarly predicted men's satisfaction.

papers.title: Micro and nanoscale probes for spatiotemporal cell analysis and manipulation.
papers.summary: This review surveys micro- and nanoscale probe technologies—fluidic force microscopy, nanopipettes, open-space microfluidic probes, and nanoneedle arrays—for minimally invasive intracellular delivery, sampling, sensing, and manipulation in living cells. It emphasizes their ability to enable repeated interrogation of the same cell, quantitative molecular delivery, and multimodal subcellular measurements, while outlining remaining engineering challenges in throughput and platform robustness.

papers.title: Information avant la lettre: The mathematical constitution of brain waves in early EEG analysis (1929-1932).
papers.journal: Studies in history and philosophy of science
papers.summary: This historical-epistemological study analyzes Günther Dietsch's 1932 paper, the first application of Fourier analysis to the EEG, showing that spectral decomposition constituted the brain trace as a decomposable causal object rather than merely describing it. It argues, via the causal-deflationary theory of information, that mathematics made the EEG trace informational before an explicit theory of information existed.

papers.title: Cathodal transcranial direct current stimulation in pediatric epileptic syndromes: mechanisms, limitations, and future research horizons.
papers.summary: This review evaluates cathodal transcranial direct current stimulation (c-tDCS) for pediatric drug-resistant epilepsy, citing meta-analytic evidence of roughly 45% seizure-frequency reduction at 4 weeks and favorable tolerability across over 600 pediatric sessions. It highlights substantial inter-individual variability, inconsistent links between interictal discharge suppression and clinical outcomes, higher modeled cortical electric fields in children, and the need for biomarker-driven selection and adequately powered trials in specific developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.

papers.title: Pediatric Headache: A Practical Approach to Clinical Diagnosis and Management.
papers.summary: This review presents a practical framework for pediatric headache diagnosis and management, organized around recognizing primary headache phenotypes, screening for secondary causes, assessing disability, and matching treatment intensity accordingly. It notes that routine imaging, laboratory testing, or EEG is generally unnecessary in typical primary headache with normal examination, and discusses multimodal acute and preventive treatment, including newer CGRP-targeted and device-based therapies whose pediatric evidence and regulatory status vary.

papers.title: Astrocyte SMN Restoration and Forskolin Treatment Improve SMA Synaptic Pathology.
papers.summary: Using human iPSC-derived astrocyte and motor neuron cultures, this study identified actin-associated filopodia defects and reduced pERM proteins in SMA astrocytes that impaired synapse formation. Dual SMN1 gene therapy plus forskolin increased astrocyte branching/filopodia and improved motor neuron synapse formation and function.

papers.title: 5-HT1A Antagonist WAY-100635 Prevents Chronic Neurodegeneration and Immune Activation After TBI
papers.summary: In a mouse controlled cortical impact model of TBI, daily post-injury treatment with the 5-HT1A antagonist WAY-100635 for 6 weeks preserved retinal ganglion cell survival and visual function, reduced microglial/macrophage activation and reactive astrogliosis, and improved motor and behavioral outcomes. Treatment did not significantly reduce cortical cavity volume, indicating preferential protection of perilesional and connected circuitry.

papers.title: Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy Aptasensors for Nucleic-Acid Detection: Advances, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
papers.summary: This review evaluates aptamer-based surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) biosensors for nucleic-acid detection, covering sensing mechanisms, plasmonic substrate engineering, aptamer immobilization, and signal amplification strategies. It reports that rational hotspot engineering and advanced amplification have enabled femtomolar to attomolar detection while discussing challenges in standardization, aptamer stability, and clinical translation.

papers.title: Step-by-Step Protocol for Fluorescence-Based Analysis of Uptake in Transporter-Expressing Xenopus laevis Oocytes.
papers.summary: This paper presents a step-by-step protocol for a fluorescence-based uptake assay in Xenopus laevis oocytes using the Arabidopsis thaliana sucrose transporter 1 (SUC1) and its fluorescent substrate esculin. The method enables rapid quantification of transporter activity via a plate reader, eliminating the need for radiolabeled compounds or electrophysiology, and is adaptable to other transporter-substrate pairs.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
